intro: Chapter 27 covers ethics and professionalism: professional codes, the four basic principles, sexual and nonsexual boundary violations, confidentiality, duties under managed care, impaired physicians, trainees, the Physician Charter (Table 27-1), common ethical questions (Table 27-2) and military psychiatry. Most rules cited are from US codes and law; update boxes add the Philippine Mental Health Act and newer standards on child-abuse reporting, case publication, the Charter's history and military confidentiality.
objectives: Tell an ethical conflict from an ethical dilemma and name the main codes.
Apply autonomy, beneficence, nonmaleficence and justice to a case.
Recognize sexual and nonsexual boundary violations.
State what confidentiality and privilege are and when confidentiality gives way.
List the psychiatrist's duties under managed care and toward impaired colleagues and trainees.
Answer the common ethical questions of Table 27-2.
